title: hunch spec
description: A judgment: rows, what the model sees, the questions it answers, and how they are tested. Reference: https://fuguai.mintlify.site/reference/spec

judgment.description: Name of the judgment; also the name of its results table.

description.description: What this judgment decides, in a sentence for people. Shown by hunch docs; never sent to the model.

model.description: The engine, pinned to an exact version: jev-1.13.0, deepseek:<id>, openrouter:<id>[@provider].

source.description: Where rows come from: a CSV path, traces(<glob>), py(<file.py>:<function>) or ref(<judgment>).

key.description: The column that identifies a row.

state.description: The columns the model sees, and nothing else.

view.description: For traces(...): one row per turn (default), per session, or per shell command.

redact.description: Removed from the state before hashing and sending: secrets, emails, home, or a regex.

clip.description: Per state column: keep the first N characters, or the last N with -N.

where.description: Keep only rows that match a condition over columns and upstream answers.

chain.description: With where: confidence becomes this judgment's own times the probability the row was routed here correctly.

weights.description: How the source rows were sampled, so every number is weighted to the population.

by.description: The column the sample was stratified by.

population.description: Each value's share of the population; shares sum to 1.

union.description: Combine one question's answers from these judgments into one table.

question.description: With union: the question the branches share.

reviews.description: Path of the reviews file, to share verdicts between judgments that ask the same question of the same rows.

on_change.description: What happens to past answers when the spec changes (default reask).

questions.description: The questions, by name. The name is not sent to the model.

tests.description: Thresholds hunch test checks, per question or metric.

metrics.description: Rules over a row, counted on answers and on gold, with misses and false alarms.

rule.description: A condition over answers and columns, as in where: destroys == 'yes' or sends_out == 'yes'.

examples.description: Rows whose answers are pinned; each is one check in hunch test.

row.description: Every state column, with the text the model should see.

expect.description: Question → answer. Quote "yes" and "no"; multi options as <question>__<option>.

exposures.description: What uses this judgment's answers (apps, hooks, dashboards, jobs). Shown by hunch docs; hunch diff names the ones a change affects.

uses.description: The questions it reads. Leave out if it reads every answer.

url.description: A link to it (http or https).

severity.description: warn: a failure prints WARN and does not fail hunch test.

type.description: choice: one option; noul: yes/no with p(yes); score: an ordered scale; multi: yes/no per option.

instructions.description: The question, with its whole meaning (the model never sees the question's name).

criteria.description: choice/multi: option → description; score: levels, lowest first; noul (optional): {"true": …, "false": …}.

none.description: choice: adds a none_of_these option, described by this text.

act.description: Below this confidence a person reviews the answer. For noul, one value or {yes: …, no: …}.

gold.description: The source column that holds the right answer, if there is one.

escalate.description: Answers below act are asked again on this engine.

min_accuracy.description: Accuracy (with reviews, the estimate) is at least this.

max_calibration_error.description: Expected calibration error is at most this.

min_act_accuracy.description: Accuracy among answers confident enough to act on is at least this.

min_auroc.description: noul: p(yes) separates gold yes from no at least this well.

order_stability.description: choice: re-ask a sample with options reordered; costs money.

min_rate.description: Metric: the rule holds on at least this share of rows.

max_rate.description: Metric: the rule holds on at most this share of rows.

max_missed.description: Metric: the missed rate is at most this.

max_false_alarms.description: Metric: the false-alarm rate is at most this.
